The pre-v1.0 A2A path. The spec moved the Agent Card to

a 2026-07 survey of 65 A2A providers found 23% still only serve the

Serves the identical card, not a second source of truth.

post.description:
A2A JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint.

Always HTTP 200: JSON-RPC carries failure in the `error` member, so
returning an HTTP error status for a well-formed call that the protocol
already has a code for would put the failure in two places and make
conformant clients disagree with us about what happened.

llms.txt (llmstxt.org convention -- not a ratified standard, but a

RFC 9727 API catalog -- a linkset document for a generic agent that
doesn't yet know anything macaroonnetwork-specific. One linkset entry
per live capability (each is independently anchored and purchasable, so
each is its own "API" per the RFC, not one entry for the whole
marketplace). service-desc always points at the shared OpenAPI document
-- there's one combined spec, not one per capability.

RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata. `authorization_servers` is
RFC 9728's own optional field (Section 2) and is omitted rather than
populated with a value -- Macaroon Network has no OAuth authorization
server, and inventing one to satisfy a scanner would make this
document false. Published purely so machine readers get a real,
minimal RFC 9728 document instead of a 404; the actual access
contract is x402 payment, documented in full at /auth.md.

schema.title: Response Oauth Protected Resource  Well Known Oauth Protected Resource Get

get.description:
Auth.md agent-registration discovery (see auth.md's own spec).
Deliberately does not claim OAuth, bearer tokens, API keys, or a
registration/claim flow this marketplace doesn't have -- an earlier
version of this route invented register_uri/claim_uri fields to
chase a third-party readiness scanner's authMd check, which made the
machine-readable surface less truthful, not more compatible. The
correct fix was publishing a real (if minimal) RFC 9728 document at
/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource that truthfully omits
authorization_servers -- see that route -- and describing the real
access model (anonymous discovery + x402 payment) honestly
here instead.

post.description: Part of the Domain Web Trust family: live TLS handshake against a domain's HTTPS port, useful for confirming a domain has a valid, current certificate before an agent interacts with a website or merchant.
